input.content: Pattern: client/consumer increment hard-requires a NEW response field that the currently-released provider does not yet emit, breaking an "independently releasable main" delivery contract. Example (enhanced-settings task 1): client.save_settings sends require_receipt:True and then `if response.get("applied") is not True: raise RuntimeError`. The released provider (provider/settings.py) returns only {"ok": True} and never sends `applied`, so every save — including ordinary non-enhanced saves the design says must keep working — raises against the deployed provider, even though the provider already persisted the data (client reports failure for a succeeded write). The accompanying unit test was edited to inject applied:True, which models the FUTURE provider and hides the backward-incompatibility (green test, broken prod). Fix: tolerate missing field for backward compat (only raise on explicit `applied is False`) or negotiate capability; add a test for the old-provider contract {"ok": True} with no `applied`. Review signal: when a diff adds a required check on a response/protocol field, verify the CURRENT released counterpart emits it, and that a test exercises the old-counterpart combination.
